newsitem.title: USA: Silverado finds gold in Alaska.
newsitem.headline: Silverado finds gold in Alaska.

text.p: Silverado Mines Ltd said it completed trenches totaling 8,300 feet on the St. Paul Gold Deposit on Ester Dome in Alaska, finding gold mineralization to a depth of at least 600 feet.

The company said the deposit has been traced for 2,500 feet of length over widths up to 300 feet and is open-ended. Preliminary tonnage and gold content based on trench assays above a 0.01 ounce gold per ton cutoff are as follows: 16,300 short tons per vertical foot 0.042 ounce per ton, or 690 ounces of gold per vertical foot. Assay values in the trenches range up to 0.59 ounce per ton.

The company said drilling showed gold mineralization to a depth of at least 600 feet, the deepest drill hole to date, with grades up to 3.5 ounces per ton. If gold were distributed to this depth the same as in the trenches, this 2,500 foot section of the St. Paul Deposit would contain over 400,000 ounces of gold contained in 9,780,000 tons. The St. Paul deposit is part of a gold mineralized regional structure that has been traced for 3.5 miles on Silverado's 20 square mile Ester Dome Property.
